title: The local relation criterion for flat fixed-coefficient sheaves
statement: Let C have objects in universe u+1 and morphisms in universe u and be essentially small in universe u+1. Let J be a Grothendieck topology on C and Λ a Noetherian commutative ring in universe u+1. Assume that forgetting Λ-module structure preserves sheaves and that sheafification equivalences of Λ-module presheaves are precisely the locally bijective maps. For a sheaf F of Λ-modules, categorical flatness (exactness of tensoring on either side) is equivalent to the following condition. For every V in C, finite family y_j in F(V), and finite matrix a_lj over Λ with sum_j a_lj y_j = 0 for every l, there is a covering sieve S on V such that for each f:W to V in S there are finitely many z_k in F(W) and b_jk in Λ with a*b=0 and y_j restricted along f = sum_k b_jk z_k. Empty families and the zero ring are included.

source.place: Section Flat modules, lemma-flat-eq, Tag 08FC, especially (3) implies (1); fixed Noetherian constant coefficients.

proof.text: Use the existing proved source theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.flat_iff_hasLocallyTrivialRelations. For the reverse implication write a tensor killed by a monomorphism as a finite sum of pure tensors and express its vanishing through finitely many linear relations. The local relation factorization makes the tensor locally zero. Thus tensoring preserves monomorphisms; it already preserves finite colimits, and is therefore exact in the abelian sheaf category. For the forward implication choose finite generators of the kernel of the finite coefficient matrix, possible over a Noetherian ring. Tensor the resulting exact sequence of constant finite free sheaves with F. A section encoding the original relation lifts locally through the kernel generators, giving the factorization matrix and sections. Sheafification and the sheafification counit identify these with the required local statements.
